model_annotations.Bulgarian: The infographic presents a hierarchical categorization of characters into three main groups: Virtual Characters, Custom Characters, and Real Characters, which are further divided into subcategories. Each subgroup is represented by a sector within a circular diagram. The diagram starts with "Virtual Characters" covering the largest portion and includes subcategories like "Informal Characters," "Comic Characters," "Movie Characters," and "Novel Characters." "Custom Characters" follows a smaller segment and is divided into "Actors," "Musicians," "Scientists," "Athletes," "Artists," and "Writers." The smallest group, "Real Characters," encompasses "Real Characters," "Game Characters," and "Influencers." The sectors do not have visible percentages or legends, and there is no mention of visual emphasis on any segment. The colors vary across subcategories, with blue for Virtual Characters, pink for Custom Characters, and green for Real Characters, without a defined scale or metric.
model_annotations.English: This pie chart categorizes various types of characters and creative professions. The chart is divided into segments representing different categories. There are 16 distinct slices, each labeled and differentiated by color and, in some cases, proportion. The main segments are "Virtual Characters," "Real Characters," and "Custom Characters," each in different shades of blue, with "New Game Characters" and "Virtual Characters" colors adding to the color diversity. Detailed slices include specific types such as cartoon characters, movie characters, video game characters, actors, and musicians. All categories are clearly labeled, and none of the slices appear to be visually emphasized over the others, such as exploded or offset segments. The total number of categories can be discerned through the individual segment labels, yet no specific percentage values are provided for each slice.
